title: trigger/first-cut 0.1.0-draft
description: Three object families: (1) the parsed TRIGGER FILE (TOML, caller-supplied via `--triggers FILE`, read as an equivalent JSON structure by tomllib; this schema describes that JSON-shaped structure, not TOML syntax itself), (2) one EVENT RECORD (JSON Lines, what an emitter reports), and (3) the FIRE REPORT `trigger_fire.py` prints. SHAPE vs SEMANTICS: this schema is shape/enum-normative for all three; the entity-ref grammar's containment rule, the per-event closed params key set, the glob grammar, and the full firing/occurrence/retrigger algorithm are cross-field/semantic rules this draft schema does not encode — `tools/trigger_vocab.py` checks those (see x-semantic-only-rules).

entity_ref.description: The entity-ref grammar. This schema only checks 'non-empty string'; the full grammar (repo id, path segment rules, resource/@self forms, containment) is semantic-only — see x-semantic-only-rules 'entity-ref-grammar'.

glob_string.description: A paths[]/src_glob entry: an authored glob pattern in a trigger's own when.params (at most 1024 characters, 64 segments, 16 '*' per segment), or a reported literal value in an EVENT record's params (at most 4096 characters, 256 segments — this schema's maxLength is the wider of the two, since a plain JSON Schema field cannot vary by which object contains it). Minimal shape check only; the full glob grammar, and which of the two size ceilings applies, is semantic-only — see x-semantic-only-rules 'glob-grammar' and 'glob-and-path-size-limits'.

when_params.description: SEMANTIC: the allowed/required key set depends on `when.event` (EVENT_VOCAB). This schema only constrains each KNOWN key's own shape when present; it does not enforce which keys are required or forbidden for a given event (that cross-field rule is enforced_by tools/trigger_vocab.py::validate_params).

trigger.description: SEMANTIC: `id` must be unique within the file — a cross-element rule this draft schema does not encode; tools/trigger_vocab.py::validate_trigger_doc checks it.

event_record.description: What an emitter reports. No emitter exists in this first cut; the exported fixtures/example event records are invented for illustration, not captured from a real emitter.

at.description: ISO-8601 UTC. Shape-only here; tools/trigger_vocab.py::parse_at is the executable norm.

error_item.description: One diagnostic emitted by trigger_validate.py or trigger_fire.py on any non-success path.

now.description: The validated --now value, or null only when no valid --now was parsed before the failure.

fire_report.description: SEMANTIC: every non-ok report, including usage and internal/input failures, has status=='unknown' and REQUIRES fired==null and suppressed==null. status=='ok' REQUIRES both to be arrays (possibly empty). `now` is null only when no valid --now was parsed. This draft schema does not encode those conditionals; tools/trigger_fire.py checks them.

run_case_report.description: Closed internal self-test envelope. Every success and error form carries the inner command status and its schema-valid fire report.

x-semantic-only-rules.description: The full entity-ref grammar: <repo> id grammar, path segment rules (no leading '/', no '.'/'..' segment, no empty segment, no '\', no control chars, no '*'/'**' outside the explicit <repo>:** whole-repo form), the resource:<name>@<host> form, and @self/@self:<path> resolution against the trigger file's own top-level `repo` field. The schema's entity_ref def only requires a non-empty string.

contains(a, b): equal; a whole-repo and same repo; a a subtree and b's path starts with that dir (same repo); a/b both resource with equal name+host. Used directionally as contains(trigger.when.source, event.source) — a cross-document rule over two different objects, which this schema cannot express.
A trigger id must be unique within one trigger file.

when.params/EVENT.params' allowed AND required keys depend on the event kind (EVENT_VOCAB) — e.g. path-changed REQUIRES paths, first-src-commit's src_glob is optional, ten event kinds allow no params at all. The schema's when_params def constrains each key's own shape but not which keys apply to which event.

Every paths[]/src_glob entry must satisfy the full glob grammar: no leading '/', no '.'/'..' segment, no empty segment, '**' only as a whole segment, each other segment restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_.*-]+.

Checked at VALIDATION, not only at firing. A trigger's own when.params glob (paths[]/src_glob): at most 1024 characters, at most 64 '/'-separated segments, at most 16 '*' characters in any one segment. An EVENT record's params (the reported literal value, not a pattern): at most 4096 characters, at most 256 segments (no '*'-count limit — '*' in a reported value is an ordinary literal character, never a wildcard).
A trigger fires on an event iff event-kind equality, source containment, AND the per-event params-match rule all hold — a three-way cross-document AND this draft schema does not encode.
occurrence_id = sha256(trigger.id + '\n' + event.event_id).hexdigest()[:32] — derived, never authored.
Duplicate redelivery (same occurrence_id already fired, in history or this run) is always a no-op, checked before retrigger==once's own second-distinct-occurrence suppression.

fired[]/suppressed[] are each sorted by (at, trigger_id, event_id) ascending — suppressed's own emitted shape (occurrence_id + reason only) does not carry the sort key, so this draft schema does not encode the ordering rule at all.
